description: GCMat, Argonne National Laboratory's Global Critical Materials model, is a dynamic agent-based model of rare earth markets, built on the Repast Simphony toolkit, that simulates individual rare earths, the permanent magnet supply chain and trade. This study uses it to test regional supply disruptions, temporary loss of production, capacity shutdown and diversion of supply, focusing on neodymium, praseodymium and dysprosium used in magnets. Disruptions tend to bring earlier mine starts outside China, some of which may not survive afterwards, market effects outlast the disruption, and the dysprosium market is strongly affected by curbing illegal supply in China. It was developed by Matthew Riddle and colleagues at Argonne, the Defense Logistics Agency and Oak Ridge National Laboratory, sponsored by the Defense Logistics Agency, and published in Resources, Conservation and Recycling, volume 164. Coverage is the global market. The accepted manuscript is available free online on OSTI; the pages read do not say whether the model is released. Caveats: scenarios are illustrative and depend on assumed capacities and behaviours. For simulation it models how shocks to critical mineral supply cascade to magnet costs for electric vehicles and wind turbines, and can test recycling, substitution and diversification. It is related to the multicommodity supply curve model record in this catalogue, another critical minerals market model.
